text:
elaine.k: FYI parcelone is seeing repeated 429s this morning on their dedicated pool. autoscaler bounced 3x in ~2m, appears to correlate with their nightly batch. opening thread to track.
support_bot: alert: tenant=parcelone pool=dedicated-eu-west spikes=3 429/sec window=60s link=https://mon.redwood/alerts/PRCL-239
omar.s: can you paste autoscaler logs and the tenant request pattern? need to know if it's noisy neighbor or legit load ramp.
devin_r: grabbing logs now, odd thing — scale decisions are alternating because the moving avg crosses threshold then a single spike drains queue and we immediately scale down.

devin_r: ```
[2026-03-16T02:12:10Z] autoscaler: pool=dedicated-eu-west decision=scale_up from=4 to=8 reason=queue>thresh queue_len=420 ma10=305 cooldown=30
[2026-03-16T02:12:54Z] autoscaler: pool=dedicated-eu-west decision=scale_down from=8 to=4 reason=idle queue_len=18 ma10=48
[2026-03-16T02:13:22Z] autoscaler: pool=dedicated-eu-west decision=scale_up from=4 to=8 reason=queue>thresh queue_len=390 ma10=310 cooldown=30
``` 

devin_r: cooldown is only 30s, so we oscillate. also our ma window is short and reacts to the instantaneous drain from batched bursts.
maria: parcelone is on a committed Dedicated plan — they're getting charged for the extra scale events, and support is getting tickets about latency and invoice surprises.
elaine.k: support asked for repro steps. parcelone runs ~2 min map-reduce style jobs hitting many long-seq generate calls. they batch thousands of small requests with short inter-arrival pauses.

omar.s: repro I ran locally: run `./tools/loadgen --tenant parcelone --pattern burst --burst-size 1200 --burst-interval 90s` and you'll see the same. sending that to perf env now.

devin_r: immediate mitigation proposals:
- increase cooldown from 30s -> 180s
- add hysteresis: require 3 consecutive windows above thresh before scale_up
- change scale_down policy to require sustained low for 2 intervals
- add tenant isolation flag (pin parcelone to a reserved slice)

maria: business ask: reduce billing churn and stop customer-facing errors quickly. pinning to a reserved slice is safest short-term.

elaine.k: agreed. plan:
1) pin parcelone to reserved-slice-12 (manual config) — rollback easy
2) tune autoscaler: cooldown=180, scale_up_hold=3, scale_down_hold=2 in canary
3) follow-up: revisit ma window to 60s and test with loadgen

deploy-bot: candidate canary config created: /infra/autoscaler/canary/parc-2026-03-16.yaml -> diff: cooldown 30->180, up_hold 1->3, down_hold 1->2

deploy-bot: canary deploy started on cluster: canary-dedicated-eu-west-3 (rolling)

omar.s: running canary load now. will validate no 429s and watch tail of autoscaler log.

devin_r: also adding a temporary per-tenant qps cap for batch endpoint (cap=1200/s) so a single tenant can't spike entire pool while we tune.
maria: support notified parcelone and offered to move them to reserved slice immediately; they're ok with short maintenance window.

elaine.k: recording follow-up tickets: ENG-5782 tune autoscaler hysteresis, ENG-5783 reserved-slice workflow, SPT-1021 bill impact reconciliation.

omar.s: can reproduce locally; with new canary config oscillation stops, scale_up occurs once per sustained burst, scale_down delays avoid immediate collapse.

devin_r: next steps: run long-run soak test overnight, if stable promote canary to global. leaving monitoring alerts for 5x repeat within 15m to notify on-call.
maria: assigning to oncall and support to keep customer loop closed. thanks team :heart:
